shape: a place named in the text read as the project's own country
input: A World Bank tender whose location field says exactly 'Georgia'. Also the bare strings Austin, Fiji, Malawi, Chad, Zambia, Bronx and 'Gambia, The'.
assertion: resolveGeography returns the country the place is in. 'Georgia' alone is the country, not the US state; 'Austin' is not Australia; Fiji, Malawi, Chad, Zambia and Gambia are themselves; Bronx is New York City. And every genuine code string still resolves: CZ010/CZE, ROU, FIN, HUN/HU322, and the extra-regio HRZZZ.
origin: Third Regional Development Project - three World Bank tenders for museum work at Stepantsminda and Mtskheta, both in the Republic of Georgia - is filed under country=United States, region_state=Georgia. It therefore sits inside every US-scoped client scope, and client-scope.audit cannot see it because the composer and the database agree about the wrong country. Two separate branches produce this: the US-state scan runs before the sovereign-country list, and the NUTS code-like branch reads the first two letters of any 3-6 character place as an ISO-2 code (Austin -> AU -> Australia, Fiji -> FI -> Finland, Malawi -> MA -> Morocco, Chad -> CH -> Switzerland). The second is the Bronx -> Brazil defect, whose fix covered only configured jurisdictions. CLOSED 2026-08-18. The branch was parts.every(codeLike), the legacy TED path, which fires on a single-word place name because one word trivially satisfies every. The old pattern accepted Austin, Fiji, Chad, Zambia, Malawi, Gambia, Queens and Bronx as codes and REJECTED the two-letter ISO2 codes it existed for. Fixed by making the shape of a real code explicit - ISO2, ISO3, or two letters plus a digit-bearing suffix, plus the literal ZZZ extra-regio marker - and by consulting the country-name table before the code table. Measured: 4 live projects and 26 live records change country; 3 records lose one, of which 2 are the Austin fix.

assertion: inCorpusScope refuses a resolved foreign country, admits the United States, and ADMITS null. An unresolved country is not a foreign one: 104 live press records resolve to no country and they include Fort Wayne and Brandywine Zoo, so failing closed on unknown would discard US coverage to enforce a rule about foreign coverage.
origin: 216 of 451 live press records had resolved outside the United States - Saudi Arabia 40, Australia 36, the UAE 33 - with no adapter pointed at any of them, so each was a headline with no filing behind it. 212 were tombstoned; 4 were held back because their own text says Austin, Texas or United States and the resolver disagreed, which is the 1H defect.

assertion: extractPressFacts returns only figures printed in the text, each with the sentence it came from; verifyNoInvention THROWS on a display string not present in the body; and factsForEntry keeps the attributed figure and drops the one whose sentence never names the project.
origin: Reading 11 articles about Heart Hotel produced 73 figures, of which 66 were about other developments: Las Vegas round-ups name the project in one paragraph and four others in the rest. Every one of those numbers was correctly read out of real text, which is what makes it dangerous - nothing about 'US$20 billion' looks wrong in a document until a reader who knows the project sees it. Attribution on single name tokens was not enough either: 'capital', 'heart' and 'anaheim' matched ordinary English and city names, so single tokens now have to identify.

shape: a number attached to a quotation that does not contain it
input: An article whose first unbroken run is longer than the 400-character sentence cap, with the figure past the cut - the OCVIBE press release opening "Back To News Press Releases Press Releases OCVIBE and Award-Winning Art and Design Studio, FUTUREFORMS, Unveil...", with "100-acre" beyond character 400.
assertion: sentenceFor caps AROUND the match rather than from the front, so every fact returned by extractPressFacts satisfies fact.sentence.includes(fact.display); and verifyNoInvention THROWS on a fact whose sentence does not contain its own display, not only on one absent from the body.
origin: The sentence cap was .slice(0, 400) from the START of the sentence, so a figure late in a long run was stored with a quotation that does not contain it. verifyNoInvention passed it because it checks the display against the ARTICLE BODY, where the number genuinely is - the right question asked of the wrong text. It surfaced only at the document boundary, where the report provenance gate refused to render the figure and failed generation of the whole August report. Three guards now: the cap is taken around the match, verifyNoInvention checks the sentence as well as the body, and report-entry drops an unquotable figure so one bad stored row cannot take out every document.

assertion: contactsFromText puts a PETITIONER value in presented_by and NEVER in applicant; a document whose only labelled name is a petitioner yields applicant null; and a document that also names an APPLICANT keeps the applicant and does not let the petitioner overwrite it.
origin: PETITIONER sat in OWNER_LABELS, so Clark County's word for the officer who BRINGS an item to the Board was read as the party behind the project. Seven records stored a county officer as the applicant and five reached a live project: Lisa Kremer, Deputy County Manager on 215 And Windmill Lane; Anna Danchik, Comptroller on the transportation bonds project; Jennifer Ammennan, Deputy Director of Comprehensive Planning on BDA South; Denis Cederburg, Director of Public Works on 163 At Casino Drive. Each printed as '[RECORD] <officer> - applicant' with a link to a county document. SAME SHAPE AS ROADMAP 1I, the Legistar sponsors finding: a sponsor answers who in government moved this item and never who is behind this project, and every one of the 24 sponsors in the corpus is an elected official or a department. Measured before the change: all 7 records the label produced are county officers and not one is a real applicant, so moving it costs nothing that was ever right.

origin: Clark agenda sheets wrap mid-clause at about 90 characters, so a department heading arrives glued to the previous bullet and a generic Title Case heading rule cannot see it. Detecting headings from a closed list fixed that and immediately caused the opposite defect: "Applicant to coordinate with Public Works - Development Review for all driveways" was cut to "Applicant to coordinate with" and opened a phantom group. A heading is always followed by the first bullet of its own list; a mention inside a sentence never is, which is what the rule now requires. Measured before and after: 140 conditions across 13 of 18 agenda sheets, 7 departments, and one truncated condition before the fix and none after.

It survived the vocabulary pass, which counts Label: occurrences and never runs the reader, and it survived a synthetic single-line test, where with spaces instead of newlines the value runs on and closes at a later label - swallowing CEQR but still matching. A tombstone that stops being written is not a tombstone.

shape: a stage read off a news report and printed as what a government body did
input: A project with eight captured filings showing holdover applications, a staff recommendation OF approval and a hearing held to 07/22/26, and fifteen press reports saying it was approved.
assertion: provenStage returns 'filed' and reports 'approved' as pressReported. A record that is not a captured filing supports 'filed' and nothing higher, and two press reports do not corroborate each other into one filing.
origin: Heart Hotel / Kulik River read 'approved' in the register and in a client document while no captured filing said so. 'approved' sits AT the unproven bar rather than above it, so stageRank(stage) <= bar admitted it from any source with no proof required and the corroboration rule was never reached. One live project of 218 changes under the fix.

shape: an element asserted while the product has removed it
input: The referral step of dashboard/e2e/report.shots.ts: 7 section removals and 8 additions fired in 1,176 ms, each starting a new report build, followed immediately by an assertion that the preview element is visible.
assertion: the referral step waits for preview-projects-count to settle before asserting report-preview exists, and asserts it with the file's own 120s timeout rather than the 20s expect default. The composer renders 'Building...' in place of the preview while any build is pending, so the element is ABSENT rather than slow.

guard.needle: THE PREVIEW IS NOT SLOW HERE. IT IS ABSENT.

origin: Reported as an intermittent referral-preview failure at report.shots.ts:302, failing once on light and once on dark. It was not a race: measured, the preview is absent for 18,335 ms after the final section edit against a 20,000 ms allowance - a margin of 1,665 ms, 8%. The only bare toBeVisible() in a file whose every other wait allows 60s or 120s. Ten more bare toBeVisible() calls exist across clients.shots, company.shots, palette.shots and project.shots and every element they name sits behind an isPending guard; they pass only because one page load resolves inside 20s.

shape: a harness slicing a list the product controls
input: The referral project picker under Simtec's scope with the Clark County chip applied: 19 projects, ordered last_activity DESC, the first with a filing in the period at position 12.
assertion: the picker loop searches the whole list. options.slice(1,12) covered positions 1 to 11 and ended one slot before the only qualifying project; off the county chip, 5 of 45 qualify at positions 11, 14, 25, 36 and 37, one of them inside the old window and in its last slot.

guard.needle: THE WHOLE PICKER, NOT THE FIRST ELEVEN.

origin: Widening Simtec's client scope to include 'filed' grew the picker past the hardcoded window. Intermittent rather than broken because the list is ordered by last_activity, so a project on the boundary crosses it whenever anything above or below it files.

shape: a project name printed under a heading that promises a geography
input: A referral brief on Heart Hotel / Kulik River, built with req.projectId set and req.geographyLabel carrying the project's name.
assertion: doc.scope.geography is the project's market or region and doc.scope.matter is its name. The running footer reads matter ?? geography, so a brief is still identified by what it is about.

guard.needle: A PLACE IN THE PLACE ROW, AND THE MATTER IN ITS OWN

origin: Every referral brief printed 'GEOGRAPHY Heart Hotel / Kulik River' three lines above a cover sentence saying the matter is in Clark County: two answers to 'where', one of them not a place. The composer and generate.ts both pass the project name as the geography label, correctly, because the footer and the delivery record want it - so the fix is a second field rather than a different caller.

shape: a filter list describing the population a document was drawn from, printed as the document's own filters
input: A referral brief for a client whose stored scope names 5 stages and 12 venue types.
assertion: the cover states the axes as a count and says what they did, in one sentence, instead of enumerating nineteen of them. The counts are printed, so standing rule 3 is satisfied by statement rather than by a list.

guard.needle: THE SCOPE AXES, COUNTED ON A BRIEF AND LISTED ON A REPORT

origin: Heart Hotel's brief printed nineteen stage and venue entries wrapping across four lines of the cover, and not one of them narrowed the document: the project id did. A recipient reads that as a document that was filtered in ways it was not.

shape: one document cited once per line instead of once per block
input: Heart Hotel's conditions block, 51 numbered lines from a single staff report; and its stated-facts block, 16 lines of which 15 share one attachment and one comes from another.
assertion: a line's citation is suppressed only when it is identical to the line immediately above. The conditions block prints one citation; the stated block prints five, at the first line and at every change of document.

guard.needle: WHICH LINES IN A BLOCK MAY DROP THEIR CITATION

origin: 51 identical copies of 'Clark County Planning/Zoning Minutes, 21 July 2026' down three pages of the referral brief, and 16 more above them. Every one correct, and the effect on the page of a document padding itself. An all-or-nothing block test was written first and rejected by measurement: it keeps all 16 in the stated block because one fact comes from a second attachment.

shape: one piece of evidence presented as several
input: Three press figures - rooms 752, storeys 29-story, site 12-acre - all read out of the same news3lv.com sentence.
assertion: figures sharing a url AND a sentence are gathered into one line carrying every label and value and the quotation once. Figures from the same article but different sentences stay apart.

guard.needle: ONE SENTENCE IS QUOTED ONCE

origin: The Heart Hotel brief printed the same forty words from one article three times in a row, once under each figure, and a reader had to compare three paragraphs to work out they were identical.

shape: a self-published post cited to a client as press coverage
input: A linkedin.com record on Heart Hotel titled Hospitality Deal Intelligence's Post, undated, held on the project alongside 15 editorial stories.
assertion: the referral press section does not quote a self-published host, and states how many items it withheld and why. The record stays captured: SELF_PUBLISHED_HOSTS answers 'may this be cited', which is a different question from JUNK_DOMAINS' 'may this be captured'.

guard.needle: CAPTURED ON PURPOSE, NEVER CITED AS COVERAGE

origin: The brief opened its press section with a LinkedIn post above the Review-Journal and the Independent, under a heading reading 'Reported beyond our record'. Measured over the 72 press records on live projects across 48 hosts: linkedin.com carries 5 and ALL FIVE ARE UNDATED, which is the shape of the thing rather than a coincidence.

shape: one withholding stated twice in two wordings
input: A referral brief whose project section prints captureSentence (24 captured, 22 printed, 2 merged) and whose coverage note also holds a mergedRecords clause.
assertion: the coverage note does not restate what the project section reconciled, and does not then claim nothing was withheld: it says where the reader will find it. The condition is on ctx.sectionIds, so a brief built without the project section still states it.

guard.needle: THE PROJECT SECTION MAY HAVE SAID THIS ALREADY

origin: The same 2 merged records were described in two different wordings four pages apart. A reader who notices reads it as two withholdings and adds them; a reader who does not thinks the document repeats itself. Suppressing it alone would have printed 'Nothing else was withheld' over a document that withheld something, replacing a duplicated true statement with a single false one.

shape: a preview that drops a whole class of content the document carries
input: The composer previewing a referral brief whose conditions section carries 51 lines in three subsections and no top-level lines.
assertion: the composer preview renders subsections, capped like the entries and stating the cap. Heart Hotel's 51 conditions are visible in the preview rather than only in the generated file.

guard.needle: THE SUBSECTIONS, WHICH THIS PREVIEW DID NOT RENDER AT ALL

origin: reports/page.tsx opens by stating that the preview IS the document - same sections, same lines, same provenance tags, same order - and rendered sec.lines and sec.entries and never sec.subsections. On a referral brief that is the conditions of approval: the single largest block in the document, and the one a referral is written for, was invisible while its heading and lede were not. Same shape as a-read-back-tool-builds-the-clients-document.

shape: a generation path that resolves a client for one target shape and not for the one beside it
input: dashboard/scripts/generate.ts with project=<name> --client=<name>.
assertion: the project branch resolves the client's scope, id, brand and addressee through the same clientTarget the client branch uses, so the membership gate reports 'enforced' and the brief matches the composer's. The project is selected out of the client's scope rather than the whole register.

guard.needle: A PROJECT TARGET MAY CARRY A CLIENT, AND USUALLY MUST

origin: project= returned base plus projectId, and base holds an empty scope and a null client id, so every referral brief this script produced was built with no client scope and the membership gate switched off. a-read-back-tool-builds-the-clients-document fixed exactly this for client= and left the branch beside it untouched. Also aligned the brand default: this script named JKR & Associates where the composer names Philip Kwong, so a Simtec document generated here carried another client's name.

shape: a migration printed, run and verified, with no code on either side of it
input: projects.stage_press_reported, created by migration 040 and confirmed applied against the live schema.
assertion: the clusterer carries provenStage's pressReported onto the project it writes, project-write persists it, and the referral entry prints stageReconcileSentence from it. A migration is done when a value reaches a page, not when the column exists.

guard.needle: COMPUTED HERE AND THEN THROWN AWAY, until now

origin: Migration 040 was run and verified on 2026-08-19. Repo-wide, the column name appeared only in the migration file and in schema-drift snapshots: nothing wrote it, nothing read it, and a query returned 0 rows carrying a value. provenStage had returned pressReported since the press-cannot-promote rule shipped and nothing carried it across. Meanwhile the Heart Hotel brief printed 'filed' above fifteen headlines saying Clark County had approved the application, with no sentence reconciling them - the exact reader-facing gap the column was created to close. Standing rule 11: a description of the work stood in for the work, and every check passed because the checks test what exists.

shape: a negative asserted from a date comparison the document's own contents refute
input: Tropicana Land resort: a schedule fact reading HELD 04/22/26, on a project holding filings dated 2026-07-21 and 2026-08-18.
assertion: the schedule line compares the date against the record set before claiming nothing came after it, and counts filings and press SEPARATELY: it says the matter filed again where a filing is later, says no filing came but a press report is later where only press is later, and claims nothing since only when nothing is.

guard.needle: NOTHING SINCE" IS A CLAIM ABOUT OUR RECORDS, SO IT IS CHECKED

origin: The referral brief printed 'That date has passed and we have captured nothing on this matter since' as a [RECORD] line, six lines above the two filings that came after it - a client document contradicting itself on the same page, in the direction that makes us look asleep. Same shape as the-honest-negative-does-not-deny-a-fact-we-hold. The FIRST fix then compared against every record and said 'the matter has filed again since' over Heart Hotel's traveltomorrow.com story, which is the RECORD/PRESS conflation the document exists to prevent, asserted on a RECORD line.

shape: a gate that is right about the exclusion and silent about it
input: A project whose only party arrives through presented_by on a filing, and a project that prints a real applicant AND has a presenter withheld.
assertion: the document states the count and the reason in both cases. noPartiesNote names the withheld bodies where the block empties, and Entry.peopleWithheldNote carries the same statement where the block still printed somebody. Neither says the filings do not identify who is behind the matter while a name is being held back.

guard.needle: AND THE SAME TRAP, ONE COLUMN OVER

origin: Measured before the presenter gate shipped: it changes the printed party list on 48 live projects and empties it on 16, and on all 16 today's noPartiesNote returned 'No party is named in the record captured for this project. The filings identify the matter but not who is behind it' - false, over a name we were holding. That is the identical defect the applicant branch of that same function was written to prevent, reintroduced one branch over by a new gate. The other 32 needed a second mechanism: noPartiesNote only speaks when the block is EMPTY, so a project that printed a real applicant and lost a presenter said nothing at all.

shape: a field set, rendered by every renderer, and never read by the section the document uses
input: A referral brief on Metropolitan Park / Willets Point, whose entry carries peopleWithheldNote naming six withheld records.
assertion: referralPeople appends the withheld note to its lines. The four renderers reading Entry.peopleWithheldNote are not enough on their own, because a referral brief's people block is built by referralPeople from e.people and never by the entry renderer.

guard.needle: AND WHAT THE BLOCK HELD BACK

origin: peopleWithheldNote was added to Entry, set in buildEntry, and rendered in doc-pdf, report-text, the composer preview and the workbook - and the referral brief printed nothing, because referralPeople reads e.people and e.noPeopleNote and never touched it. Metropolitan Park lost 'Deputy Mayor for Housing and Economic Development' from its parties and said nothing about it. Found by generating the brief and reading it, not by a test: standing rule 11, a field that exists is not a sentence that prints. The market report was correct throughout, which is why nothing failed.

shape: a fixed pause standing in for a settle wait, read as the thing it waited for
input: openClientView in membership.audit: goto /projects, click a client, await the scope bar, then count [data-row-id].
assertion: the row list is polled until two consecutive reads agree before the caller counts it. The scope bar and the row list are separate queries, so the bar being visible says nothing about the list having been replaced.

guard.needle: POLL, DO NOT WAIT AND READ

origin: waitForTimeout(2500) then read. Run alone the audit reads 45 rows and passes in 38s; run in sequence behind the other walkthrough audits, one worker and one browser on a loaded machine, it read FIFTY - exactly the register's page size, which is the unscoped list it was still showing. The membership counts were identical in both runs (31 proposed, 5 confirmed, 10 excluded = 46), so the assertion 46 >= 50 failed and a push was REFUSED on a harness race rather than on anything in the tree. This file already names the defect forty lines further down - 'POLL, DO NOT WAIT AND READ. A fixed pause followed by one read is the stale-result defect this brief spent a part on' - and fixes it in its revert loop while leaving it in its own opening helper. Same family as a-harness-waits-for-the-rebuild-it-caused: a fixed pause is a bet on how long something takes, and the suite loses that bet under load.

shape: a role that means something different, rendered identically to the roles beside it
input: The Players screen listing companies whose only company_projects role is 'presenter' - 15 of the 47 government bodies the document layer withholds, including Lisandro Orozco, the Rent Guidelines Board and the Borough President of Queens.
assertion: the presenter role is marked on the row - its own token, muted, with a title saying it is who moved the item in government - and a row whose ONLY role is presenter carries data-presenter-only. No filter, no deletion, and the companies table is untouched: the extraction is recording a true fact and this screen is not a client document.

guard.needle: A ROW WHOSE ONLY ROLE IS PRESENTER IS NOT A PLAYER

origin: The presenter gate landed in the document layer (people.ts) and the Players screen reads a different layer entirely - fetchPlayers over companies and company_projects, never buildParties - so the gate had no reach there. Measured: 15 of 47 movers present as companies, every one under role='presenter', 18 of 132 live links. They rendered as 'presenter' in a comma-joined string beside 'applicant' and 'representative' with nothing marking the difference. Labelled rather than gated because the two questions are different: a government body printed as somebody to call in a CLIENT DOCUMENT is a correctness defect, and the same fact on Philip's own surface is worth knowing - the Borough President of Queens moving two matters is useful here precisely because it is useless in a brief. Muted rather than accented because screens.shots enforces a per-screen accent budget and this screen spends its one accent on reachability.

shape: a headline number that counts artefacts
input: The companies table at 267 rows, quoted as a corpus fact alongside 211 links and 1 cross-market firm.
assertion: the count is stated after removing what is not a name and what is the same row twice. 267 rows hold 1 form label ('Approved By'), 9 byte-identical duplicate pairs, and 257 distinct named companies - of which 177 have a link to a live project.

guard.needle: IT DOES NOT DECIDE WHAT A NAME IS

origin: Measured 2026-08-20. Two findings contradicted the assumption behind the question. The OCR debris 'Robert C. Lopane, RLA L, So«t,e,s-' is NOT in the companies table at all - it sits in presented_by on a Westchester lead and reaches a document without reaching the count. And the near-duplicate spellings are not spellings: all 9 groups are byte-identical strings inserted twice, and there are ZERO genuine spelling variants in 267 rows, so the SPV caution - two near-identical names are routinely two different entities - is the right caution with nothing to bite on. Brooklyn Borough President is not a duplicate either: the second row is 'Brooklyn Borough President on behalf of the Brooklyn...', a different filing posture. Nothing was merged or removed; identical strings are safe to merge mechanically but that is a write to the companies table and wants its own printed migration.

shape: one jurisdiction's document reader assumed to generalise to another's
input: Three real City Planning Commission reports (250108, 240092, 250046) passed to readFilingFacts from readers/clark-agenda-sheet.
assertion: the Clark conditions extractor is NOT applied to CPC reports, and readers/cpc-report reads only what a CPC report states unambiguously - applicant, decision, recorded vote exceptions - and no conditions. A conditions reader for legal resolutions is its own build.

guard.needle: IT DOES NOT READ CONDITIONS, AND THAT IS A DECISION RATHER THAN AN OMISSION

origin: New York carries ZERO conditions corpus-wide while one Clark County project carries 51, and the obvious move was to point the existing extractor at the New York equivalent. Measured before building: it returns 0, 5 and 0 conditions over three real CPC reports, and the 5 are an accident of one report containing a literal 'CONDITIONS:' line. It keys on CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL headings, bullet characters and a CLOSED LIST OF EIGHT CLARK COUNTY DEPARTMENT NAMES. Clark publishes an ADMINISTRATIVE CHECKLIST; New York publishes a LEGAL RESOLUTION - RESOLVED clauses and obligations in prose, 8 occurrences of 'shall' across 163 pages. Building a second reader keyed on RESOLVED would be a New York special case; a reader for legal resolutions is a different and more general thing, and would reach any jurisdiction that publishes decisions that way. COST IS NOT THE OBSTACLE and was measured too: a CPC report costs a median 497ms to fetch and parse against 1,883ms for a Clark staff report, and the 163-page one parses in 327ms - all 13 reachable reports would cost about 6.5 seconds.

shape: a count of who spoke read as a count of who voted
input: CPC report 250108, which contains 'in favor of the application and 11 in opposition' (public testimony) and 230070, which contains 'in favor, none opposed and none abstaining' (the COMMUNITY BOARD's vote).
assertion: the vote fact is built only from the Commission's own exception markers - Commissioner, VOTING NO | ABSTAINING | RECUSED | ABSENT - which appear nowhere else in the document. 'In Favor' is never read as the Commission's vote.

guard.needle: AND THE ONE I REFUSED

origin: Every CPC report contains the phrase 'In Favor' and in none of the seven examined is it the Commission's vote: it is public testimony or the community board's recommendation. A pattern keyed on it would have printed a community board's 11-24-8 as the City Planning Commission's decision on a client document. ALSO FOUND while verifying: the Commission abbreviates itself, and 250224 reads 'duly adopted by the CPC' where six others spell it out - a pattern keyed on the full name returned nothing for it and the fact was silently absent rather than wrong, which is the missing-entry-deletes shape.

shape: a source stating a fact in prose that we may not act on without a name rule
input: Seven CPC reports read for their IN THE MATTER OF applicant: five private, one public authority (The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey) and one city agency (the New York City Department of City Planning).
assertion: the applicant is written UNGATED, exactly as every other untyped applicant is. The reader does not decide whether a party is public, because the only available signal is the name and a name-shape rule is the label-read-as-the-thing-it-names defect. If a New York source ever publishes an applicant type the way ZAP publishes applicant_type, that is the fix.

guard.needle: THE APPLICANT IS WRITTEN UNGATED, DELIBERATELY

origin: A CPC report says in plain English that the applicant is the Department of City Planning, and the system cannot use that without reading the name. applicant_type is published by ZAP alone; null means the source did not say, never that the applicant is private, and untyped applicants are ungated everywhere else - so gating here would be inconsistent AND would require the forbidden rule. Measured after wiring: the decision cost nothing, because ZERO projects gained an applicant. Every ZAP record carrying a ULURP number already had one, and the reader never overwrites a structurally-stated fact with a second reading of a different document, so neither public body was ever written.

shape: a fact built from parts and offered as verbatim evidence
input: The first version of readCpcReport, whose commission_action display was built as `adopted ${date} (Calendar No. ${n})` and whose the_vote display was `1 voting no, 1 abstaining`.
assertion: every FilingFact display is a verbatim substring of the document and of its own line, which is what verifyFilingFacts enforces. The counts are a reading and go in `value`; the display is the document's own words.

guard.needle: THE CAPTURED GROUP IS THE DISPLAY, AND IT MUST BE VERBATIM

origin: Caught by running the reader's output through the real verifyFilingFacts before wiring it, rather than by reading the code: all 13 facts would have been rejected. The guard exists so a client can check a value against the filing it is printed beside, and a reassembled string cannot be checked that way even when every component of it is true. After the fix, 7 of 7 reports passed the guard and 13 of 13 records were written with zero rejections.

shape: a captured value cut by a counter rather than by its own end
input:
The Anaheim agenda text 'Categorically Exempt from the provisions of the California 
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State 
CEQA Guidelines Section 15301, Class 1 (Existing Facilities) and Section 15315, Class 15 (Minor Land Divisions). 
Approved continuance...'
assertion: the stored ceqa_class display is the whole sentence up to '(Minor Land Divisions)' and never 'Categorically Exempt from the provisions of the California'. Every clipped value is a verbatim PREFIX of the matched text, so it stays a verbatim substring of the document.

guard.needle: THE FIRST SENTENCE END, NOT THE LAST

origin: A client brief printed 'CEQA: Categorically Exempt from the provisions of the California.' Two rounds of fixing the wrong thing: widening the 60-character window changed nothing, and cutting at the LAST full stop produced '...(Minor Land Divisions). Approved Resolution No' - a cut inside 'No.', worse than the truncation it replaced. The cause was found only by fetching the source document: the agenda is a table column wrapped every eight words, norm() keeps newlines by design, and every prose pattern written with [^\n] stopped at the first wrap. Fixing the wrap did not only untruncate one value, it recovered two fields that were silently absent corpus-wide: environmental 0 -> 10 of 12 records (83%) and action_sought 0 -> 3 (25%).

shape: a detector's result read as a different claim than the one it supports
input: An Anaheim council record whose captured text opens 'Adoption of resolutions dedicating municipal property for public streets, public utilities and other municipal purposes' in English and continues with the Spanish twin of the same item.
assertion: the note 'Spanish-language record; no English capture of this item' requires BOTH Spanish markers present AND English markers absent. A bilingual capture prints its English and says nothing, because nothing has been withheld.

guard.needle: AND THE COUNTER-TEST, BECAUSE SPANISH FOUND IS NOT ENGLISH ABSENT

origin: Measured: THREE records on live projects carry Spanish markers and ALL THREE are bilingual, so the note fired every time it fired and was wrong every time. The marker test answers 'is there Spanish in this text'; the note claimed 'we hold no English capture'. Same shape as the six defects standing rule 8 was written for.

shape: a cap discarding what there was room to print, and stating a reason that was not the reason
input: OCVibe's stated block: eleven printed facts under a total cap of 24, with the line '2 further stated figures held back to keep this list readable.'
assertion: the per-kind cap orders the block rather than trimming it. Over-cap values go after the breadth pass and print where the total cap leaves room, so 'held back' is said only when the block is actually full.

guard.needle: THE PER-KIND CAP DEMOTES, IT DOES NOT DELETE

origin: Two things wrong in one sentence: two facts were thrown away with thirteen places free, and the reason printed was length when the cause was breadth. The breadth rule itself is kept - it is the Metropolitan Park fix, where ordering by importance alone filled the block with four hearing dates before reaching the 250-room hotel.

shape: one class of conflicting evidence reconciled in prose while another prints bare
input: OCVibe's press block: $5 billion, $4B and $1 billion for amount reported; 100-acre against 20 acres for site; 5,000-seat against 300-capacity for seats.
assertion: where a press label carries more than one value, the block prints a sentence naming the labels that disagree, stating that each figure is quoted from the article that printed it, and stating that no filing states any of them - so the reader is told it is a disagreement between sources rather than a correction of one by another.

guard.needle: disagreementNote

origin: The stage got a reconciliation sentence this week and figures did not, so a reader met three project costs on one page with nothing to tell them the three are different claims. Ranked by the reader as the second of seven read defects. The disambiguator built for repeated labels reduced them from 18 projects and 40 labels to 5 and 8, and all 8 residual are press figures, which is this.

shape: a document naming a contact and leaving the reader's next question unanswered
input: Tropicana Land's people block: 'Holland & Hart LLP - representative, contact named in the filing. 5470 Kietzke Lane #100, Reno, NV 89511. No phone or email in the record.'
assertion: where a party carries no phone, no email and no separate firm line, the negative also states that no other name is given alongside it. The sentence types nothing: it is as true of a firm with no partner named as of an individual with no firm.

guard.needle: HOW THE RECORD SAYS TO REACH THIS PARTY, INCLUDING WHEN IT DOES NOT

origin: The obvious fix was to detect that Holland & Hart is a firm and say so, and it is refused: a name cannot be told from a firm in this corpus - the shape rule consolidates 4 identities and misreads 31 company names as people - and inferring a type from a name is the defect standing rule 8 exists for.

shape: a recovered value trusted because the fetch succeeded
input: 43 records on live projects whose title ends in a search result's ellipsis, re-fetched for the page's own og:title.
assertion: a fetched title is written only where it BEGINS with the head already held, compared on letters and digits alone. Where it does not, the record keeps its ellipsis.

guard.needle: THE GUARD, AND WHY IT IS THE WHOLE POINT

origin: 31 of 43 recovered and verified, 3 refused, 9 unreachable. All three refusals were genuinely wrong pages: one site front page ('OCVIBE | The new heart of Orange County'), and two edited headlines that no longer match what the search result carried. Without the guard all three would have been written as the record's headline. Also measured first: the full headline is NOT recoverable from what we already hold - 4 of 43 head-matched a stored body, and two of those bodies carry their own ellipsis, because capture:press-bodies stores a Serper description rather than an article.
